## Answers to exercises 05

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import tifffile as tiff

import skimage as sk
from skimage.util import invert
from scipy import ndimage
```

## Bacterial data

The code below uses the same building-block strategy from chapter 05a and then
loops over all frames.

```{python}
def _global_mask(input_img, disksize_range=20):
    img_min = ndimage.minimum_filter(input_img, footprint=sk.morphology.disk(disksize_range))
    img_max = ndimage.maximum_filter(input_img, footprint=sk.morphology.disk(disksize_range))
    img_delta = img_max - img_min

    thresh = sk.filters.threshold_otsu(img_delta)
    mask_global = img_delta > thresh
    mask_global_fill = ndimage.binary_fill_holes(mask_global)

    labeled_global = sk.measure.label(mask_global_fill)
    largest_region = np.argmax([r.area for r in sk.measure.regionprops(labeled_global)]) + 1
    mask_global_filled = labeled_global == largest_region

    border_margin = 5
    disksize_shrink = max(0, disksize_range - border_margin)
    mask_global_final = sk.morphology.erosion(
        mask_global_filled,
        footprint=sk.morphology.disk(disksize_shrink),
    )

    bbox = sk.measure.regionprops(mask_global_final.astype(int))[0].bbox
    return mask_global_final, bbox


def _get_edges(input_img_crop, sigma_smooth=3, disksize_crossing=1):
    img_gauss = sk.filters.gaussian(input_img_crop, sigma=sigma_smooth)
    img_laplacian = sk.filters.laplace(img_gauss)

    edges_min = ndimage.minimum_filter(img_laplacian, footprint=sk.morphology.disk(disksize_crossing))
    edges_max = ndimage.maximum_filter(img_laplacian, footprint=sk.morphology.disk(disksize_crossing))
    mask_edges = np.logical_and(edges_min < 0, edges_max > 0)
    return mask_edges


def _bacterial_seeds(input_img_crop, min_distance=5):
    img_smooth = sk.filters.gaussian(input_img_crop, sigma=3)
    seed_locations = sk.feature.peak_local_max(img_smooth, min_distance=min_distance)
    return seed_locations


def _flood_fill_multiple(mask_edges, seed_locations):
    mask_filled = mask_edges.copy()
    for x, y in seed_locations:
        mask_filled = sk.morphology.flood_fill(mask_filled, (x, y), 2)
    return mask_filled


def _unique_seeds_distance(mask_bacteria, sigma_seed=3, distance_threshold=3):
    distance_map = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(mask_bacteria)
    distance_map_blur = sk.filters.gaussian(distance_map, sigma=sigma_seed)
    mask_seeds = distance_map_blur > distance_threshold
    return sk.measure.label(mask_seeds)


def seg_bacterium(input_img):
    mask_global, bbox = _global_mask(input_img, disksize_range=20)

    input_img_crop = input_img[bbox[0]:bbox[2], bbox[1]:bbox[3]]
    mask_global_crop = mask_global[bbox[0]:bbox[2], bbox[1]:bbox[3]]

    mask_edges = _get_edges(input_img_crop, sigma_smooth=3, disksize_crossing=1)
    seed_locations = _bacterial_seeds(input_img_crop, min_distance=5)
    mask_filled = _flood_fill_multiple(mask_edges, seed_locations)

    mask_bacteria = np.logical_and(mask_filled, mask_global_crop)
    mask_unique_seeds = _unique_seeds_distance(mask_bacteria, sigma_seed=3, distance_threshold=3)

    result = sk.segmentation.watershed(-1 * mask_bacteria, markers=mask_unique_seeds, mask=mask_bacteria)
    return result
```

```{python}
# Put the location of the data here.
path_ecoli_data = "/Users/m.wehrens/Data_notbacked/2025_Py-Image-workshop_Filamentation-example-data/pos3crop_timelapse_switch890.98.tif"

# Load data
imgs_ecoli = tiff.imread(path_ecoli_data)

# Loop over all frames and segment
segmasks_ecoli = []
mean_areas_ecoli = []

for t in range(imgs_ecoli.shape[0]):
    current_segmask = seg_bacterium(invert(imgs_ecoli[t]))
    segmasks_ecoli.append(current_segmask)

    props_t = sk.measure.regionprops(current_segmask)
    areas_t = np.array([p.area for p in props_t])
    mean_areas_ecoli.append(np.mean(areas_t) if len(areas_t) > 0 else np.nan)

# Store masks and summary values
np.savez_compressed(
    "output-test/ecoli_pipeline_results.npz",
    segmasks=np.array(segmasks_ecoli, dtype=object),
    mean_area=np.array(mean_areas_ecoli),
)

# Plot observed bacterial areas over time
plt.figure(figsize=(9 / 2.54, 5 / 2.54))
plt.plot(mean_areas_ecoli, lw=1)
plt.xlabel("Frame")
plt.ylabel("Mean bacterial area (px)")
plt.title("E. coli: segmented area over time")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Nuclear data

### Segment nuclei and extract nuclear KTR signal for a single image

```{python}
def seg_nuclei(input_img):
    thresh = sk.filters.threshold_triangle(input_img)
    mask = input_img > thresh
    mask = sk.morphology.remove_small_objects(mask, min_size=60)
    mask = ndimage.binary_fill_holes(mask)
    result = sk.measure.label(mask)
    return result


# Path used in earlier chapters
img_path_KTR = "/Users/m.wehrens/Data_notbacked/2025_Py-Image-workshop_KTR-example-data/raw/Composite_KTR.tif"
img_KTR = tiff.imread(img_path_KTR)

# Single frame
t0 = 0
img_nuclei_t0 = img_KTR[t0, 0]
img_ktr_t0 = img_KTR[t0, 1]

segmask_nuclei_t0 = seg_nuclei(img_nuclei_t0)

props_t0 = sk.measure.regionprops_table(
    segmask_nuclei_t0,
    intensity_image=img_ktr_t0,
    properties=("label", "mean_intensity", "area"),
)
nuclear_ktr_t0 = props_t0["mean_intensity"]

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12 / 2.54, 5 / 2.54))
axs[0].imshow(img_nuclei_t0, cmap="gray")
axs[0].contour(segmask_nuclei_t0 > 0, levels=[0.5], colors="r", linewidths=0.5)
axs[0].set_title("Nuclear segmentation")
axs[0].axis("off")

axs[1].hist(nuclear_ktr_t0, bins=20)
axs[1].set_xlabel("Nuclear KTR signal")
axs[1].set_ylabel("Count")
axs[1].set_title("Single-frame per-nucleus means")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Extract nuclear KTR signals over time

```{python}
def ring_mask_for_label(labeled_nuclei, label_id, ring_width=4):
    nucleus_i = labeled_nuclei == label_id
    if not np.any(nucleus_i):
        return np.zeros_like(nucleus_i, dtype=bool)

    ring_i = sk.morphology.binary_dilation(nucleus_i, footprint=sk.morphology.disk(ring_width))
    ring_i = np.logical_and(ring_i, labeled_nuclei == 0)
    return ring_i


n_frames = img_KTR.shape[0]

segmasks_nuclei = []
all_nuclear_signals = []
all_ring_signals = []
mean_nuclear_signal = []
mean_cytoplasmic_signal = []
ratio_nuc_cyto = []

for t in range(n_frames):
    img_nuclei_t = img_KTR[t, 0]
    img_ktr_t = img_KTR[t, 1]

    segmask_t = seg_nuclei(img_nuclei_t)
    segmasks_nuclei.append(segmask_t)

    props_t = sk.measure.regionprops_table(
        segmask_t,
        intensity_image=img_ktr_t,
        properties=("label", "mean_intensity", "area"),
    )

    labels_t = props_t["label"]
    nuclear_signal_t = props_t["mean_intensity"]
    ring_signal_t = np.full_like(nuclear_signal_t, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for i, lab in enumerate(labels_t):
        mask_ring_i = ring_mask_for_label(segmask_t, lab, ring_width=4)
        if np.any(mask_ring_i):
            ring_signal_t[i] = np.mean(img_ktr_t[mask_ring_i])

    all_nuclear_signals.append(nuclear_signal_t)
    all_ring_signals.append(ring_signal_t)

    mean_nuc_t = np.nanmean(nuclear_signal_t) if len(nuclear_signal_t) > 0 else np.nan
    mean_cyto_t = np.nanmean(ring_signal_t) if len(ring_signal_t) > 0 else np.nan

    mean_nuclear_signal.append(mean_nuc_t)
    mean_cytoplasmic_signal.append(mean_cyto_t)
    ratio_nuc_cyto.append(mean_nuc_t / mean_cyto_t)

# Store masks and summaries
np.savez_compressed(
    "output-test/KTR_pipeline_results.npz",
    segmasks=np.array(segmasks_nuclei, dtype=object),
    mean_nuclear=np.array(mean_nuclear_signal),
    mean_cytoplasmic=np.array(mean_cytoplasmic_signal),
    ratio_nuc_cyto=np.array(ratio_nuc_cyto),
)

# Plot nuclear and cytoplasmic signal over time
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14 / 2.54, 5 / 2.54))

axs[0].plot(mean_nuclear_signal, lw=1.2, label="Nuclear")
axs[0].plot(mean_cytoplasmic_signal, lw=1.2, label="Cytoplasmic ring")
axs[0].set_xlabel("Frame")
axs[0].set_ylabel("Mean KTR signal")
axs[0].set_title("KTR signal over time")
axs[0].legend()

axs[1].plot(ratio_nuc_cyto, color="k", lw=1.2)
axs[1].set_xlabel("Frame")
axs[1].set_ylabel("Nuclear : cytoplasmic")
axs[1].set_title("Nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

A likely interpretation is that kinase activity changes over time.
When activity is higher, KTR tends to shift to cytoplasm, so the
nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio tends to decrease.

## Background correction

```{python}
# Simple correction strategy from chapter text: subtract a per-frame mode.

def mode_uint(img):
    img_u = img.astype(np.uint16)
    return np.argmax(np.bincount(img_u.ravel()))


bg_values = np.array([mode_uint(img_KTR[t, 1]) for t in range(n_frames)], dtype=float)

mean_nuclear_signal_bg = np.array(mean_nuclear_signal) - bg_values
mean_cytoplasmic_signal_bg = np.array(mean_cytoplasmic_signal) - bg_values
ratio_nuc_cyto_bg = np.where(
    mean_cytoplasmic_signal_bg > 0,
    mean_nuclear_signal_bg / mean_cytoplasmic_signal_bg,
    np.nan,
)

plt.figure(figsize=(9 / 2.54, 5 / 2.54))
plt.plot(ratio_nuc_cyto, label="Raw ratio")
plt.plot(ratio_nuc_cyto_bg, label="Background-corrected ratio")
plt.xlabel("Frame")
plt.ylabel("Nuclear : cytoplasmic")
plt.title("Effect of background correction")
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
